      "observations": [
        "All 28 owned paths and all 1,302 historical diff lines were read, including Cargo metadata, handwritten transport and generator changes, all generated path/type hunks, both complete new generated files, and all three affected test functions.",
        "The Operation API changes from build(&self) with an associated Body to build_request(self) returning Result<Request<Vec<u8>>, Error>. The generated builder serializes OperationBody::JSON with application/json or moves OperationBody::Other bytes and the caller's content type. GET/next-page/delta operations use empty byte vectors. Serialization and HTTP-builder errors become explicit Result paths, while generated URI parsing still contains unwrap; the patch does not remove every panic path.",
        "The generator generalizes PATCH emission to POST and imports the body property's type. The emitted changes add mail-folder POST and /me/messages GET/POST, a message collection response, and Serialize on the changed property-map types. send_mail_request_body.rs is changed but removed from the generated module list and supported-type list; this does not implement a /me/sendMail operation.",
        "Original XpComGraphClient uses the request's method instead of hard-coded GET. A nonempty byte body requires a present, string-valid Content-Type and is passed to moz_http; an empty body skips both body setup and that header check. Only Authorization and the selected body content type are explicitly bridged here, not every arbitrary header on http::Request.",
        "moz_http replaces its custom Method with borrowed http::Method and sets the native request method after upload setup. Consuming the operation avoids the old body clone at builder construction, but this is not an end-to-end zero-copy or memory benchmark claim: accepted set_body explicitly copies bytes for stream lifetime. The current body documentation and original OperationBody example spell plain/text; the builder accepts the supplied string without validating a specific RFC822 media type.",
        "The three changed Rust tests build selected GET, next-page and delta continuation URIs and compare them with expected URIs; their response-value assertions are also preserved. They add no direct POST/Other/header/error assertion. All five assert_eq! calls in these affected functions omit an expected-behavior message; expect/panic strings do not supply assertion messages.",
        "Accepted source retains consumed JSON/Other request construction in a moved generated paths/me/messages.rs module and an expanded generator. Its Graph client now builds requests before queued dispatch and awaits the queue/result channel. These are later phases; no direct original transport lifetime, sending success, batching performance or network authorization is inferred.",
        "Generated output has explicit overwrite markers and compact generated grouping; style observations remain scoped to generator versus handwritten code. The handwritten request builder's body-before-method comment explains ordering. The old OperationBody::JSON doc points to Operation::build, while accepted source corrects it to build_request; no broad documentation convention is inferred.",
        "Full required Bug 2011672 current0–2/activity/footer and D286212 creation-to-final timeline were read from exact Parent/C3 originals. All six actual old/current inline bodies and actual summary Old(empty)/New pair were read, including declared drive-by method/receiver/name/error-message changes.",
        "The reviewer raises the distinction between no body and an empty body. The author explains that graph_xpcom manually extracts request fields and skips body setup for an empty Vec, then adds the Operation comment. Owned client and trait code confirm that exact behavior; acceptance does not establish HTTP/2, reqwest or all Graph-server equivalence.",
        "The author considers an alternative-body allow-list but chooses the broader escape hatch, including possible third-party/beta uses; actual OperationBody::Other is available to the generated body-bearing operations. Those possible consumers are proposals, not executed compatibility. Other/Custom naming is open-ended discussion; source retains Other. build_request consumes self and generated builders own serialization, while native transport copying remains a distinct scope.",
        "Historical rustfmt defects precede later completed builds, but final landing occurred with ongoing/failed builds and a subsequent remote failure. No fresh generation, test, lint, HTTP request, RFC822 encoding or Graph action occurred. Upstream reqwest/thiserror documentation, OpenAPI/server claims and Bug2013310 bodies remain bounded unread dependencies.",
        "The preferred source only adds a focused public lesson for the already inspected five message-less Rust assertions and absent direct POST/body tests. Existing source objects/timestamps remain identical; no extra source or runtime credit is claimed."
      ],
